title: Smallest Keyword Cover
statement:
Find the shortest contiguous part of a word stream that contains every required keyword.

Contract
- `words` and `keywords` are non-null arrays containing non-null strings. `keywords` contains distinct values.
- Return a two-element array `{left, right}` for the shortest inclusive range in `words` that contains every keyword at least once.
- If several ranges have the same minimum length, return the one with the smallest left index.
- Return `{-1, -1}` when no range covers all keywords. If `keywords` is empty, return `{0, -1}`.
- Words not in `keywords` may appear inside the returned range.

Examples
- In `[a, b, c, a, b]` with keywords `[a, c]`, return `[2, 3]`.
- In `[alpha, beta]` with keywords `[gamma]`, return `[-1, -1]`.
- In `[one, two, three]` with no keywords, return `[0, -1]`.

examples.input: words = [a, b, c, a, b], keywords = [a, c]

hints: Use a sliding window with left and right boundaries over the word array.
Keep counts only for keywords currently inside the window, plus how many distinct keywords are covered.
Whenever all keywords are covered, try shrinking from the left before expanding again. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(k) space.
inputSyntax: Input: words list, then keywords list, for example: [a, b, c, a, b] [a, c]
